key_insight: IRT can help summarize AI benchmark performance, but its rankings and item estimates become unreliable when benchmark conditions differ from the human-testing setting it was designed for.
engineering_relevance: For benchmark designers and evaluation engineers, the study shows that estimator choice and dataset regime can directly affect model rankings, predicted scores, and item diagnostics.
method: Simulated response matrices from six widely used LLM benchmarks using three common IRT models.
Compared four estimation approaches: marginal maximum likelihood, MCMC, variational inference, and a neural pseudo-Siamese estimator.
Tested reliability, scalability, and computational feasibility across 18,000 benchmark conditions.
evidence_signal: Across 18,000 simulation conditions, classical estimators sometimes became infeasible at benchmark scale, while scalable methods could produce poor item-level and ranking inferences for small or nonnormal model sets.
watch_item: IRT outputs may look precise even when the model set is too small, skewed, clustered, or multimodal, so diagnostics are needed before trusting benchmark claims.
paper_title: Can We Trust Item Response Theory for AI Evaluation?
